required_outcomes: Asks the tenants in writing (email and/or SMS) whether someone will be home for the plumber on Monday 21st October in the afternoon, or whether the provider may collect the office key instead.
Does not arrange key collection or entry with the office key before the tenants have agreed.
Keeps the job moving while waiting: puts it on hold for the tenants (or schedules a follow-up) with a review date before Monday 21st.
acceptable_alternatives: Replying to the provider first to acknowledge the Monday 21st PM booking and say access is being confirmed with the tenants, then asking the tenants.
Recording the Monday 21st PM slot as provider-confirmed with access 'tenant_home' only if the agent also asks the tenants and states that access is not yet confirmed.
positive_behaviours: Mentions the pets at the property to the provider or asks the tenants about them for access.
Uses a second channel (SMS) because the tenants have not returned the provider's voicemail.
Gives the tenants a way to propose another time if Monday 21st PM does not suit.
red_flags: Escalating to a human for a routine access question the tenants can answer.
Telling the tenants the plumber will let himself in with the office key if they do not reply.
prohibited_actions: Telling the provider to collect the office key for Monday 21st before the tenants have agreed.
critical_failures: Authorising entry with the office key without the tenants' agreement or at least 24 hours' written notice.
Ending the turn without asking the tenants about access, so the Monday 21st booking stalls.
